tips.title: No "a", "the" or plurals
body: Chinese has no words for "a" or "the", and nouns never change for plural: 苹果 is "apple", "an apple", "the apples".
Verbs don't change either: 我要 (I want), 你要 (you want), 他要 (he wants).

tips.title: 的: "'s" and "my"
body: Put 的 after a person to show what belongs to them: 我的 (my), 你的 (your), 妈妈的 (mom's).
With family and home, 的 is often dropped: 我妈妈, 我家.

tips.title: Measure words: 一个
body: A number can't go straight before a noun. A measure word goes in between: 一个姐姐 (one older sister), 三个苹果.
个 (ge) is the all-purpose one. Others depend on the thing: 本 for books, 只 for many animals, 杯 for cups. 一 changes tone before them: yí ge, yì běn.

tips.title: 很 + adjective: no 是 needed
body: To describe something, put the adjective right after the subject, usually with 很: 我的房间很大 (my room is big).
Don't use 是 here. Said lightly, 很 is just the link ("is"); stress it to mean "very".

tips.title: 了 for a new situation
body: 了 at the end of a sentence says something has changed: 我饿了 (I'm hungry now), 吃饭了 (it's time to eat).
It's about a new state of things, not just the past.

tips.title: 想 and 要: wanting
body: 想 + verb is "would like to, feel like": 我想玩. 要 is stronger, "want, going to": 我要回家.
To say no, put 不 before it: 我不想.

tips.title: 没有: "don't have"
body: 有 (to have) is the one verb you can't negate with 不. Say 没有 instead: 我没有哥哥.
Every other verb takes 不 for "don't": 我不喜欢.

tips.title: 吗: yes-or-no questions
body: To turn a statement into a yes-or-no question, add 吗 at the end: 你喜欢狗 → 你喜欢狗吗？
To answer, repeat the verb: 喜欢 (yes) or 不喜欢 (no). There's no single word for yes.

tips.title: 两 for "two" before a measure word
body: When you count things, "two" is 两, not 二: 两只猫 (two cats).
二 is for counting out loud and in bigger numbers (十二, twelve).

tips.title: Question words stay in place
body: Chinese questions keep the order of the answer. Put the question word where the answer would go: 这是猫 → 这是什么？ 他是老师 → 他是谁？
Don't add 吗 to a question that already has a question word.

tips.title: 在 + place + 上 / 下 / 里
body: To say where something is: thing + 在 + place + position word. 书在桌子上 (the book is on the table).
The position word comes after the place: 上 on, 下 under, 里 in.

tips.title: Yes-or-no questions with "A not A"
body: Another way to ask yes or no: say the verb or adjective, then 不, then again. 远不远？ (is it far?), 好不好？
The 不 in the middle is said lightly.

tips.title: 会: can (a skill you learned)
body: 会 means "can" for things you've learned: 我会说中文 (I can speak Chinese).
能 is "can" in the sense of being able or allowed: 你能帮我吗？

tips.title: 太…了 and 一点儿
body: 太 + adjective + 了 means "too …": 太贵了 (too expensive).
Adjective + 一点儿 means "a bit more …": 便宜一点儿 (a bit cheaper), 大一点儿的 (a bigger one).

tips.title: Time comes before the verb
body: When something happens goes before the action, right after the subject: 我七点起床 (I get up at seven).
How you go somewhere also goes first: 我坐地铁上班 (I take the subway to work).

tips.title: 了 after a verb: it happened
body: 了 right after a verb marks a finished action: 我去了公园 (I went to the park), 我看了一部电影.
To say it didn't happen, use 没 and drop 了: 我没去.

tips.title: 又…又…: both … and …
body: 又 A 又 B describes two qualities at once: 他又高又瘦 (he's tall and thin).
长得 + description says what someone looks like: 她长得像她妈妈.

tips.title: …的时候: when, while
body: Put 的时候 after an action to say "when" or "while" it happens: 我做饭的时候 (while I was cooking).
已经…了 is "already": 他已经走了 (he had already left).

tips.title: 去不了: can't manage to
body: Verb + 不了 says something can't happen: 我去不了 (I can't go). Verb + 得了 is the opposite: 去得了.
不好意思 is the soft way to apologize or turn something down.

tips.title: 如果…就…: if … then …
body: 如果 starts the condition and 就 introduces the result: 如果下雨，我们就待在家里.
…怎么样？ at the end makes a suggestion: "how about …?"

tips.title: 从…开始: since
body: 从 + time + 开始 says when something started: 我从昨天开始发烧 (I've had a fever since yesterday).
Pain is just body part + 疼: 我头疼.

tips.title: Giving advice
body: 应该 is "should", 最好 is "you'd better", and 我建议你 is "I suggest you".
要是我是你 (if I were you) is followed by 我会… (I would …).

tips.title: 被: something done to you
body: 被 marks something bad that was done to the subject: 我的钱包被偷了 (my wallet was stolen).
The doer can go after 被: 被小偷偷了 (stolen by a thief).

tips.title: 说得对: how well something is done
body: Verb + 得 + description says how something is done: 你说得对 (you're right, lit. you said it right), 他跑得很快.
This 得 is pronounced de, with no tone.

tips.title: 虽然…但是… and 一方面…另一方面…
body: 虽然 (although) is paired with 但是 (but) in the second half. Unlike English, Chinese uses both: 虽然很难，但是值得.
一方面…另一方面… balances two sides of an argument.

tips.title: 你 or 您?
body: 您 is the respectful "you" for older people, customers, bosses and strangers in formal settings. 你 is for everyone else.
People are often addressed by surname + title: 王总 (Director Wang), 李老师 (Teacher Li).

tips.title: 把: doing something to something
body: 把 moves the object before the verb when you do something to it: 把盐递给我 (pass me the salt).
It's very common in requests and instructions.
